mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over a 3-month period signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the quarterly GDP level exceeds 17000 billion (2017 dollars) and housing starts exceed 1400 thousand units, it signals a robust economic expansion that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (GDPC1>17000 and HOUST>1400) holds for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by CPIAUCSL > 250, FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, and UNRATE > 5.0%), a high CPI reading signals persistent inflation that may lead to central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The late-cycle regime condition holds (CPIAUCSL>250, FEDFUNDS<0.5%, UNRATE>5.0%) but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: The level of retail sales (RSAFS) is positively correlated with equity market returns; higher RSAFS levels are associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS is above its 5-year moving average but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market and weak economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0% but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) are both above their respective 5-year moving averages, it signals a strong consumer and housing market that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS are both above their 5-year moving averages but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery regime (defined by PAYEMS > 140000 and UNRATE < 8.5%), a rising employment level signals improving economic conditions that support equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The labor market recovery regime condition holds (PAYEMS>140000 and UNRATE<8.5%) but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.
